title: Forecast allocation versus hydrologic realization under competing claims

dependency_gate.implementation_rule: No DUMMY-15B model or tests before DUMMY-15 qualification and baseline rebinding.

purpose: Reproduce the original conflict where management allocation sees enough predicted surface-water capacity, but later shared-state hydrology reduces the physically realizable managed withdrawal.

stage_contract.forecast_capacity: M_pred is an explicit allocation-stage capacity estimate; first canonical forecast ignores surface-groundwater exchange and uses A_s*(h_s0-hmin).
stage_contract.allocation: Split min(R_root+R_ext,M_pred) lexicographically by the declared managed priority. Record allocated_root and allocated_ext.
stage_contract.realization: Submit only the allocated total to the qualified shared-state physical management oracle. It returns supplied total M_actual and physical exchange V.
stage_contract.realization_split: Split M_actual lexicographically using the same declared priority, with each supplied claim additionally capped by its allocated amount.
stage_contract.commit: Only supplied flows and physical exchange enter the water ledger and accepted states. Allocated-but-unsupplied water is diagnostic only.

invariants: sum supplied_i equals the exact coupled realized managed total for the allocated request
allocated-but-unsupplied volumes do not enter any physical storage balance
physical exchange V is not clipped to protect allocation
root state changes by supplied root irrigation, not allocated root irrigation
combined three-store storage change equals minus supplied external demand when root external forcing is zero

forecast.interpretation: surface-only storage above hmin appears sufficient for both managed claims

underallocation_control.purpose: Show that actual physical capacity may exceed the allocated total; realization must not create unallocated managed delivery.

hypotheses: The canonical surface-only forecast allocates the full 60 m3, but exact shared-state realization supplies only 32 m3 because physical exchange consumes 28 m3 while satisfying the management threshold.
Priority-preserving realization curtails lower-priority allocated claims before higher-priority allocated claims.
Root-first and external-first canonical cases have the same actual total managed withdrawal, V, surface endpoint and groundwater endpoint, but different supplied splits and root memory.
Allocated-but-unsupplied water never appears in the combined ledger or root endpoint.
When forecast allocation is below what the physical system could realize, supplied flow cannot exceed allocated flow.
Changing M_pred changes allocation and may change the realized physical endpoint because the physical layer only attempts the allocated managed flow, but it cannot cause supplied_i > allocated_i.
A forecast error is a management-information error, not a license to alter the physical exchange law.

public_authority_binding.note: Current public documentation distinguishes demand, allocated and supplied. DUMMY-15B remains a one-Basin analytical realization oracle and does not claim exact Ribasim physical-layer curtailment semantics.

forbidden: no claim that priority-preserving realization is current Ribasim supplied-flow behavior until executable Ribasim evidence is obtained
no network routing or allocation fairness
no production SWAP irrigation authority claim
